description: Expected results for GemPy's official anticline (fold) example model: gempy/API/examples_generator.py::_generate_anticline_model with gempy_data jan_models/model2 CSVs (extent 0-1000 m, octree refinement 5, one series Strat_Series = rock2, rock1). inputs/ are the unmodified CSVs from cgre-aachen/gempy_data commit cf00bc9.
engine_version: gempy 2026.0.1a2.dev0+ge46fee77b (git e46fee7, tag v2026.0.1a1 line), gempy_engine 2026.0.1a0, numpy backend

official_reference_check.what: 51 scalar-field values sampled every int(n/50)-th point of the finest octree level centers (octrees_output[-1].outputs_centers[0].exported_fields.scalar_field), exactly as test/test_model_types/test_example_models_I.py::test_generate_fold_model does
official_reference_check.source: cgre-aachen/gempy git e46fee7: test/test_model_types/test_example_models_I.test_generate_fold_model.Anticline Scalar Field.approved.txt (unmodified copy)
official_reference_check.tolerance_source: GemPy's own test/verify_helper.py ArrayComparator (np.allclose rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-5)

numeric_checks.name: n_finest_level_points
numeric_checks.why: number of finest-level octree centers the official test samples from

numeric_checks.name: lith_block_size
numeric_checks.why: 32^3 cells of the refinement-5 regular block

numeric_checks.name: lith_count_id1
numeric_checks.why: cells of unit id 1 (rock2) in the lithology block

numeric_checks.name: lith_count_id2
numeric_checks.why: cells of unit id 2 (rock1, the folded layer)

numeric_checks.name: sf_finest_min
numeric_checks.why: min scalar field on finest octree level

numeric_checks.name: sf_finest_max
numeric_checks.why: max scalar field on finest octree level

numeric_checks.name: sf_finest_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean scalar field on finest octree level

numeric_checks.name: parse_n_groups
numeric_checks.why: KI parse tool reads one structural group from the saved model

numeric_checks.name: parse_n_elements
numeric_checks.why: KI parse tool reads two surfaces (rock2, rock1)

numeric_checks.name: parse_grid_n_points
numeric_checks.why: KI parse tool reads the 32768-point grid

finished_check: driver exits 0 and prints DRIVER_OK after gp.compute_model and gp.save_model
reference: Main check = GemPy's own approved array (official). numeric_checks = values from our own run; two clean runs gave byte-identical results (deterministic).
notes: Only change from the official generator: the CSV paths point to local copies in inputs/ instead of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cgre-aachen/gempy_data/master/... (same bytes, checked by sha256 against commit cf00bc9). The run matches the official approved values to about 5e-9 (the approved file is printed with 8 decimals). Lithology ids 1,2,3 follow the stack order rock2, rock1, basement.
